Meta-learning aims to create algorithms capable of acquiring new tasks with limited data by leveraging a large collection of tasks during training. This paper investigates meta-learning within the framework of linear representation learning, grounded in the well-established linear ELR model widely used in deep learning theory. We demonstrate that meta-gradient descent, a meta-learning algorithm, can successfully optimize a small number of task-specific parameters using few examples, provided there exists a task-agnostic linear representation that effectively maps inputs to task labels across all tasks. Furthermore, we prove that meta-gradient descent can discover this optimal representation by optimizing a generative task model, even when task distributions vary significantly. Consequently, we present a joint optimization method for both task parameters and their shared representation, showing that this approach can identify a nearly optimal representation even with highly divergent task distributions. Our numerical experiments confirm the efficacy of both methods in linear representation learning, highlighting their potential for real-world generalization beyond synthetic linear models. Additionally, we present an example of applying these methods to natural image classification. Finally, we establish an upper bound on generalization error for both approaches, providing insights into the sample complexity required for training. Overall, this work offers a theoretical foundation for meta-learning representation, supported by both theory and numerical experiments. While Massively Multilingual Models enable state-of-the-art machine translation systems to overcome data scarcity in low-resource languages, their superior performance often results in excessively large models that are impractical for deployment. Knowledge Distillation and Quantization offer promising strategies for creating effective multilingual models that balance accuracy, robustness, and model size. This study evaluates the impact of progressive quantization and distillation on monolingual British-to-Finnish translation. Our findings indicate that combining finetuned quantized teacher models with student models can distill up to 95% of accuracy while reducing model size by 15%. Additionally, we demonstrate that monolingual models exhibit greater robustness during quantization compared to multilingual architectures. Finally, we illustrate how these techniques facilitate the development of a high-performing FinnFAS model capable of processing FinnFAS data without any FinnFAS-specific training data. The source code is accessible at https://github.com/JoelKorhonen/too-brittle-to-touch. Utilizing Pegasus, T5, FinFAS, and QFinnFAS data, we demonstrate how quantization and distillation enable the creation of high-performing multilingual models without the need for language-specific training data. Our results show that students trained solely on British English can achieve state-of-the-art results on Finnish test sets. This success is primarily attributed to the robustness of Pegasus and T5 models when utilizing FinnFAS pretraining and quantization. Furthermore, we demonstrate that post-pruning and quantization allow for the creation of highly effective single-stream encoder-decoder models that are 20 times smaller than their teacher-finnFAS counterparts. We anticipate that our methodology and findings will inspire researchers to pursue similar approaches, potentially leading to more efficient mass-multilingual models in the future. Finally, we show that combining FinnFAS with Pegasus and T5 models can achieve the highest test-set performance on British-to-Finnish translation.

We introduce a new class of hypergraphs constructed through the iterative application of two mappings within the unit square. By associating each hypergraph with a specific irrational number derived from the fixed point of a Lagrangian density function for a single hypergraph, we demonstrate that the densities of these graphs across a sequence approach the derivative of this function at a point within the unit interval. Furthermore, we establish that the Lagrangian density governing the growth of hypergraph sequences exhibits singularities at two irrational points in the unit interval, which are fixed points of this function, thereby providing an affirmative resolution to Jacobsthal's problem. Additionally, we formulate a system of function equations involving two irrational variables and analyze the continuity of its solution. Finally, we illustrate an algorithm for generating pairs of irrational numbers based on the fixed points of this Lagrangian density function.

Although image captioning has advanced significantly, current models often produce captions lacking in detail and controllability. To address this, we introduce Prompt Captioning, a novel framework that incorporates prompts into the captioning process. Specifically, we investigate prompt-based fine-tuning on pre-trained vision-and-language pre-trained models, demonstrating through multiple experiments that it substantially improves the model's ability to generate more detailed images. Furthermore, our approach allows for the easy integration of various prompts to enhance description control, enabling the generation of more diverse and context-aware captions. Additionally, we present a prompt-learning method that facilitates the generation of multi-perspective descriptions. Extensive evaluations on diverse datasets confirm the effectiveness of our method. Zero-shot neural machine translation enables a model trained on a source language to directly translate into a target language without any in-domain training data. In multilingual speech-based systems, this approach is highly attractive for supporting low-resource languages. This study addresses the underlying challenge by tackling speech translation and evaluating zero-shot translation capabilities across eight languages. We analyze four data scenarios and examine four models to propose three novel methods for enabling zero-shot speech translation. Experimental results indicate that our proposed techniques can produce effective zero-shot translations for nearby languages. Additionally, we demonstrate that these methods can achieve state-of-the-art performance in few-shot settings across a broad language family. We have made our code and data available at https://github.com/MLforSDG/speech-translation. Accurate short-term energy consumption forecasting is vital for grid stability, yet this is particularly challenging in low-voltage networks where solar generation and energy storage are prevalent. These distributed energy resources are often installed at the household level, making it difficult to predict their impact on the grid. Consequently, it becomes essential to forecast not only total energy usage but also energy peaks and their timing. This paper introduces a deep learning model designed to predict the number of peaks and the duration of the longest peak. Additionally, it explores the integration of probabilistic forecasts through a novel loss function specifically for FCR-NC (Full Data for Net Counter) data. By incorporating peak timing information, the accuracy of peak duration predictions is enhanced. For instance, under weather-dependent conditions, the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) is reduced by 17% compared to a deep learning baseline without weather data, and by 26% relative to the ground truth. This represents a significant improvement, amounting to a 30% reduction in RMSE compared to the best-performing model. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that utilizing the information content within probabilistic load forecasts can substantially boost the accuracy of predicting peak behavior. Numerous machine learning algorithms have emerged recently, offering a vast array of options for addressing specific tasks. While selecting appropriate methods is well-documented, determining how best to incorporate existing knowledge remains less clear. This paper offers a comprehensive overview of design choices when integrating knowledge, particularly focusing on data, features, and prior knowledge. It begins by defining "knowledge" within the context of machine learning and data mining. Subsequently, it presents an extended framework illustrating when and how to apply these design choices through a PACT model (Purpose, Assumptions, Consequences, Tradeoffs). Finally, the study explores how these choices influence the design of machine learning competitions and concludes with a roadmap for future research in this area. The findings are validated by examining a specific case study on multi-label classification in medical imaging. Overall, this work serves as a valuable resource for practitioners and researchers, providing a solid foundation for effectively leveraging data and domain knowledge in machine learning applications. The proposed framework is also broadly applicable to other data-driven tasks, such as natural language processing and computer vision. These annotations are often unavailable or prohibitively costly and time-consuming to obtain. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a data-efficient framework that relies solely on a few manually labeled images and an extensive corpus of unlabeled data. Accurate localization and identification of vertebrae are essential for numerous clinical tasks involving spine analysis, including surgical planning, preoperative assessment, and radiation therapy. This study introduces a method to automatically localize and identify vertebrae in spine CT scans. The approach utilizes an anatomically-constrained optimization framework that integrates an initial localization estimate derived from a small number of landmark annotations. Specifically, we apply a 3D sphere packing model to estimate fiducial vertebral bodies, which serves as a robust prior for localization. Additionally, we employ an anatomically-based regularization term that enforces a minimum inter-vertebral distance, leveraging the known fact that the inter-vertebral distance maximum occurs near vertebra 5. To achieve efficient and accurate localization, we utilize a global 3D optimization method. For identification, we map the localized vertebrae onto a common template using an initialization strategy based on observed displacement patterns, followed by an iterative alignment process using a linearized affine registration. Experimental results across a large-scale dataset demonstrate the method's robustness, showing superior performance compared to state-of-the-art approaches in both vertebra localization and identification. Furthermore, the method's ability to reliably localize and identify vertebrae using sparse annotations underscores its potential for clinical applications. The source code is publicly accessible at https://github.com/leeyang1992/VertebraLoc.

Recent nature-inspired machine learning approaches have enhanced quadrupedal locomotion by utilizing actual dynamic actuator elasticity. While the superior performance of these agents compared to static elasticity models is widely recognized, the specific learning behaviors that enable this exploitation remain unexplored. In this study, we demonstrate that dynamic actuators enable better locomotion by allowing agents to generate greater ground reaction forces during high-speed running. Furthermore, we find that strong dynamic actuators offer advantages over weak ones, even when both can perform crouching movements. Finally, we validate the importance of elasticity exploitation by comparing agents trained on real actuators with those trained on UNO, a common elastic torque actuator. Our findings indicate that UNO's limited force output restricts the benefits derived from elasticity, ultimately degrading locomotion performance. To our knowledge, this is the first research to address the "why" behind the significance of dynamic actuator elasticity in quadrupedal locomotion training. This short paper introduces a novel, computationally sound method to characterize quantum separability for an arbitrary number of qubits. Our approach reformulates the quantum separability problem using density matrices as decision variables and implements it within the framework of variational quantum algorithms. The resulting variational algorithm explicitly characterizes separability for a given multi-qubit density matrix $\rho$ by computing the success probability of a specific single-shot measurement on $\rho$. Leveraging existing quantum hardware, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for systems comprising up to three qubits. Notably, for a two-qubit system, the method yields a direct criterion for separability that is equivalent to the well-known positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion. Furthermore, the proposed criterion can efficiently detect certain types of entanglement in systems with an odd number of qubits, where no PPT-based criterion exists. Additionally, the method exhibits robustness against experimental imperfections, such as qubit decoherence and control inaccuracies. Finally, we outline a path to characterize entanglement in many-qubit systems by determining the entanglement threshold for a family of problems. These problems involve identifying the minimum weight of a non-separable convex combination of pure product states that matches a specified family of symmetric, multi-qubit mixed states. The entanglement threshold for any given problem can be directly derived from a classical computational problem known as the vector coloring problem, a variant of the famous graph coloring problem. Furthermore, the entanglement threshold for these problems can be accurately approximated by solving a graph relaxation problem that transforms the integer programming vector coloring problem into a linear programming one. The derived thresholds serve as many-qubit extensions of entanglement criteria based on indecomposability and reduction criteria. Moreover, many of these problems can be further relaxed by removing the unitary constraint, thereby connecting them to the prominent graph state quantum tomography problem. Finally, the proposed method is also applicable to continuous-variable quantum systems. In such systems, we demonstrate that the variational algorithm can characterize separability for Gaussian states by optimizing over Gaussian states within the variational problem. This demonstrates that our approach is also applicable to continuous-variable quantum systems. In such systems, the method can determine separability for Gaussian states by optimizing over the set of Gaussian states in the variational problem. Slab plasmas characterized by a decaying magnetic field and a narrow current sheet often exhibit small-scale tearing modes, which can trigger the collisionless tearing instability and lead to magnetic reconnection. This phenomenon is prevalent across various space and laboratory plasma environments. While extensive theoretical research has traditionally focused on tearing modes within constant-width collisionless current sheets, this work examines the distinct characteristics of such modes in smoothly formed, narrow, and narrow-banded current sheets. Both ideal and non-ideal modes are investigated through numerical simulations and analytical formulas. The study demonstrates that in these specific conditions, the most unstable ideal tearing modes exhibit three key traits: they are significantly narrower and more elongated than those in narrow-banded scenarios; they are anchored deeply within the current sheet rather than residing near X-points; and they display lower growth rates. Conversely, ideal tearing modes with the highest growth rates remain broad and are not deeply embedded in the current sheet. Furthermore, it is established that for both ideal and non-ideal modes, the real part of the wavenumber remains real, and the mode does not manifest as a kink. Instead, it appears as a helical perturbation that widens over time while maintaining a constant magnetic flux. These broadening modes are localized near X-points and generate magnetic islands. The findings suggest a potential mechanism for the formation of magnetic islands and the onset of quasi-separatrix layers (QSLs) in smoothly formed, narrow, and narrow-banded collisional collisionless slab plasmas. Additionally, these results may contribute to understanding magnetic reconnection processes within magnetic braids. Finally, the implications of these results are extended to the broader context of magnetic braids. These insights could aid in interpreting observations of magnetic braids in the Sun, such as those seen in solar flares and coronal mass ejections, as well as in other space and laboratory settings. Ultimately, this research offers a novel perspective on the physics of magnetic reconnection. Keywords: magnetic reconnection, tearing mode, QSL, magnetic braids.

This paper addresses Fashion Image Search (FAIS), focusing on two critical challenges: (1) the scarcity of annotated images, and (2) the difficulty of separating image-level attributes (IA) from feature-level attributes (IA). To address these issues, we introduce a novel approach that integrates semi-supervised learning with attribute disentanglement. This solution comprises three core components: (1) a semi-supervised learning framework utilizing semi-supervised autoencoders to enhance performance with limited labeled data; (2) a regularized disentanglement mechanism ensuring that IAs remain independent within the hidden layers; and (3) an interpolation layer designed to manipulate IAs for improved semi-supervised retrieval. Experimental results on the FIGURE dataset demonstrate that our method surpasses existing baselines. This work addresses finding the $\R$-minimizing solution to the linear ill-posed equation $Ax=y$ within a Banach space, where $x \in \R \subset B$, $\R$ denotes the range of a convex, even, lower semicontinuous function $\R$, and $y$ belongs to the range of $A$. We introduce a dual gradient algorithm to solve this operator equation and demonstrate its finite convergence under suitable conditions on the initial data. Additionally, we prove the convergence of the algorithm when the starting point is selected randomly according to a specific probability distribution. Finally, we illustrate the methodology using examples from sparsity promotion and entropy minimization. As an application, the derived results enable the efficient and accurate recovery of signals from few noisy measurements. Furthermore, the proposed algorithms are shown to be equivalent to two existing methods: the gradient flow for the convex envelope and the dual gradient flow for the entropic prior, both originally motivated by applications in compressed sensing. Constructing matching costs is a fundamental component of light field (LF) depth estimation. Conventional approaches typically compute these costs independently for each sub-aperture image, often neglecting inter-image relationships and the critical factor of occlusion. This paper introduces a cost constructor that is both occlusion-aware and aware of relationships across multiple sub-aperture images. Specifically, we develop a recurrent cost constructor that sequentially integrates multiple virtual views to generate aggregate sub-aperture cost volumes, ensuring that contributions from all views and accounts for occlusion are considered. Furthermore, we propose a multi-subspace recurrent cost constructor that integrates information across different sub-aperture images to produce a multi-subspace cost volume, enhancing robustness against occlusion. Experimental results on the 4D-STEM and LF-Datasets-1 and 2 demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in LF depth estimation. Additionally, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness and efficacy of this proposed constructor. The code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/zhonghaohao/LFNet.

This paper examines the Fokas-Lenells equations using a bilinear method. We first bilinearize the system to derive novel multisoliton and multi-solitary wave solutions via the residue method. Subsequently, we transform the bilinear system back into the original dependent and independent variable form to generate novel wave solutions. The paper concludes by providing examples of multisolitons, solitons, solitary waves, and shock waves to demonstrate the method's efficacy. Furthermore, we illustrate that the Fokas-Lenells equations admit multiple soliton interactions of varying orders, including both elastic and inelastic, highlighting their capacity to produce diverse nonlinear effects. These findings offer a new perspective on the Fokas-Lenells model, which has recently garnered significant research interest. Finally, we suggest potential applications of these solutions in plasma physics. Finally, it should be noted that this bilinear approach offers a straightforward and efficient pathway for constructing multisoliton solutions for integrable nonlinear partial differential equations. **Keywords:** Fokas-Lenells equations; multisoliton solutions; nonlinear partial differential equations; plasma physics. **AMS Subject Classification:** 35Q53; 35C06; 35C08. **Corresponding author:** Dr. Mohammed Al-Khasawneh (email: mohammed.al.khasawneh@yarmouk.edu.jo). **Affiliation:** Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Science, Yarmouk University, Karama, Jordan. **Date:** 2021-07-13. **DOI:** 10.22052/jam.2021.3750. **ISSN:** 1735-7536. **Journal:** Journal of Advanced Mathematics, Volume 37, Number 5, 2021, Pages 1119-1133. **URL:** http://www.jam.journals.ir. **Published:** 2021-07-13. **Received:** 2020-09-10. **Accepted:** 2021-01-11. **Available online:** 2021-07-13. **Language:** English. **Type:** Article. **Category:** Research. **Section:** Partial Differential Equations. **Pages:** 1119-1133. **DOI:**

Non-Riemannian gravity frameworks describe spatially unresolved riemorphic fields via the spatial components of a mixed symmetric tensor. Specifically, the spatial metric and an additional field known as the riemorphic raptor metric characterize vortical gravity. This work demonstrates that a splicing action for this vortical gravity framework, derived from the double field theory (DFT) action, is consistent and maintains Weyl invariance. Furthermore, the paper calculates the field equations and establishes a correspondence with the non-Riemannian gravity action proposed by S. Deser and A. Jackeli. Additionally, the spatial decomposition of the DFT action is performed, revealing a novel non-Riemannian ghost-free spatial non-Riemannian gravity theory. Finally, the paper concludes with remarks on non-Riemannian black holes and their relationship to light and geodesics. Notably, this study represents the first instance of utilizing DFT to investigate non-Riemannian gravity theories. This paper introduces a novel, completely distributed algorithm designed for identifying suitable access points (APs) for a roaming station within the IEEE 802.11 family. Existing 802.11k/v frameworks enable AP discovery and traffic congestion management but lack a direct mechanism for load-aware selection. This short contribution addresses that gap by developing a new AP selection algorithm that considers total link load between two stations. The algorithm is fully distributed, computationally efficient, and easy to implement. To evaluate its performance, we developed a simulation platform that models an indoor home network, simulating key 802.11k/v features and the proposed method. Our results demonstrate that this load-aware selection algorithm significantly outperforms traditional distance-based or signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)-based approaches. This improvement is particularly evident in dense networks featuring many overlapping APs with high user density. We also compared the computational complexity of our proposed algorithm against existing 802.11k/v specifications and found that it remains less complex. Finally, we validated the effectiveness of the 802.11k/v framework in both urban and home environments. To achieve this, we developed an Extender Selection Algorithm (ESA) compatible with 802.11k/v, which is fully distributed and allows for efficient network-wide optimization of the extender placement problem. This work was partially funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research (MIUR) under grant PRIN 2017/2018 (grant number: 2017J22C59). Extensive simulations were conducted to verify the proposed algorithm's efficacy. The source code is available at: https://github.com/AndreaBartolini94/Extender-Placement-Algorithm.
